Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module 5 on energy storage devices on fuel cells.

Key details

  • In a thermal power plant, we know that combus of fuel is done and power is generated from there.
  • But this happens in several steps.
  • When the fuel burns, there is heat generated.
  • This thermal energy is used to run turbines.
  • These turbines now are used to generate power.
  • To electrical energy, but at each step there is a loss of efficiency.
  • The idea in a fuel cell is can we convert the chemical energy directly into the electrical energy?
  • If that is done.
  • We will definitely have a better efficiency, and that is exactly what is done in a fuel cell.
  • The chemical energy is directly converted into electrical energy, and we find that the efficiency is about 75 to 80 percent.
  • Hydrogen is the fuel and oxygen is the oxidant is done in the form of galvanic cell.
  • We can see very clear hydrogen is getting oxidized to water and oxygen is getting reduced to water.
  • So therefore, we know that combustion of a fuel it is a redox reaction.
  • And we know in a galvanic cell we can use this redox reaction.
  • How we can make the reaction happen in two different compartments, meaning that we will not allow the hydrogen and oxygen to come in contact, but we will allow the hydrogen to undergo oxidation at the anode and oxygen to undergo reduction at the cathode.
  • Since hydrogen is undergoing oxidation.
  • At the anode electrons will be generated and these electrons are going to move through the external wire towards the cathode where there is oxygen and that is going to absorb the electrons and undergo reduction.
  • So whatever is the chemical energy of the fuel oxygen system is getting directly converted into electrical energy by means of a redox reaction.
  • And they are they undergo reaction, and that is how we get power from the battery.
  • But a fuel cell, though it is also a galvanic cell, is different from a battery.
  • Because the fuel and the oxidant, that is the electroactive material, have to be supplied.
  • Continuously from outside as at the respective electrodes.
  • Fuel cell, the fuel and the oxidizing agents have to be continuously supplied.
  • They will be able to generate power only as long as the electroactive material is supplied at the anode and the cathode.

Example or application from the lecture

  • The combustion of fuel, that is, say for example, hydrogen and oxygen.
  • Let us check whether the combustion of fuel is a redox reaction.
